data.body:
ALL ACs DELIVERED AND MERGED. Evidence recorded here in a COMMENT (box state is normalized
out of the material fingerprint and is attestation-safe; annotating the AC text would not be).

MERGED to main:
  ade954fcd3  heal a stranded index on foreign paths      (landed previously)
  ab0e7f577f  stop using the shared stash stack           (change 1584)
  19341e2edb  report source paths polluting the tracker   (change 1585)
  <1588>      add the supported tracker-maintenance door  (change 1588)

AC1 — NO git stash operation in the tickets worktree.
push.py performs `git stash create` (a stash COMMIT OBJECT; refs/stash untouched), then
`reset --hard`, merge, and `git stash apply <sha>`. Verified there is no remaining
`stash push` / `stash pop` / `stash drop` call site; the `stash drop` at the old push.py:200
is gone because there is nothing on a stack to drop.

AC2 — provably scoped so it can never apply another worktree's entry.
Scoping is structural rather than asserted: the restore names OUR OWN commit by sha, so
there is no stack to consult and no branch-of-origin check to get wrong.

AC3 — held-out test, tests/interfaces/store/test_push_shared_stash_2fa6.py.
It encodes the RACE, not the steady state: LIFO ordering alone hides the bug because an
uncontended pop does take its own push. A foreign source-worktree stash is injected BETWEEN
the set-aside and the restore. PROVEN RED on the parent commit — the raced stash is applied
and src/raced.py materializes inside the store, reproducing the incident — and GREEN after,
with refs/stash left byte-identical (both foreign entries present, neither popped nor
dropped) and no unmerged index entries.

AC4 — the regenerable-files assumption is ENFORCED, not assumed.
_resolve_conflicted_pop became _resolve_conflicted_apply. It classifies each conflicted path
with gitutil.path_is_foreign_to_branch and routes both buckets through discard_unmerged_paths:
a path the tickets branch TRACKS is restored from HEAD; a path it does NOT track cannot be
ticket data, so it is removed AND logged at warning level rather than vanishing silently.

AC5 — fsck reports a tracker holding tracked-source paths.
FOREIGN_STORE_PATH is a COUNTED issue (non-zero exit), not a WARN, and names separately any
stray the branch actually TRACKS — those were committed and will propagate on the next push.
Classification is single-sourced as fsck.foreign_store_path_list so the repair acts on exactly
the set the report names.

AC6/7/8 — the supported door, the break-glass, and the docs.
`rebar tracker-maintenance [--status|--clean] [--force=<reason>]`:
  * backup ref refs/rebar-maintenance/<utc> at HEAD BEFORE the first write, printed with its
    rollback command (the predecessor tagged mid-run, which is what made it useless);
  * REFUSES on unpushed ticket commits, making NO writes at all — backup ref included — and
    failing CLOSED when origin/tickets is missing, because local commits cannot then be
    proven safe. Treating 'unknowable' as zero would defeat the guard;
  * durable JSONL audit in the tracker's GIT DIR (actor from git identity, argv, backup ref,
    unpushed count, forced flag + reason, paths touched) — deliberately not the worktree, so
    it can never become store content a later merge conflicts on;
  * --force=<reason> requires a written reason (bare --force exits 2), is loud on stderr, and
    is recorded as forced:true.
Docs state the rule and name the break-glass: AGENTS.md pointer, docs/concurrency.md
§"Mutating the tracker: no AD-HOC raw git", cli-reference.md (generated), exit-codes.md.

RESIDUAL RISK — unchanged and worth carrying forward.
The incident needed (1) rebar stashing in the tickets worktree — NOW FIXED EVERYWHERE by this
change — and (2) a foreign stash on the shared stack. Condition (2) is still reachable in any
environment whose tracker is a LINKED WORKTREE (the old default); this machine's is now a
standalone clone and the reviewbot clones (Dockerfile.reviewbot:154). Other dev machines and
CI checkouts remain UNAUDITED. With AC1 shipped, rebar itself no longer creates the hazard,
but an operator running `git stash` by hand in a linked-worktree tracker still can.
